extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners representing trademark applicants before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing competent, ethical, and compliant practice by attorneys (including sponsorship and signature practices) before the USPTO in trademark matters, and the sanctions/conditions that follow violations. Focused on representation, electronic filing, supervision, responses to OED, and conditions of suspension/probation/reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Counsel Rule (37 C.F.R. § 2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective August 3, 2019, any foreign-domiciled trademark applicant or registrant must be represented before the USPTO by an attorney who is licensed to practice law in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule was intended to (1) increase compliance with U.S. trademark law and USPTO regulations, (2) improve the accuracy of trademark submissions to the USPTO, and (3) safeguard the integrity of the U.S. trademark register. See Requirement of U.S. Licensed Attorney for Foreign Trademark Applicants and Registrants, 84 Fed. Reg. 31498 (July 2, 2019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark signature requirements (37 C.F.R. § 2.193)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark signature rules require that (a) all signatures on trademark documents be signed by a proper person, (b) trademark documents be personally signed by the signatory named on the document, and (c) a person electronically signing a document must personally enter any combination of letters, numbers, spaces, and/or punctuation marks adopted as a signature and place that combination between two forward slash ("/") symbols in the signature block on the electronic submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.193(a), (c), and (e); and 37 C.F.R. § 11.18(a). Noncompliance may render the submission improperly executed and unable to support registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMEP electronic-signature guidance (TMEP § 611.01(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents must be personally signed. The person identified as the signatory must manually enter the elements of the electronic signature; another person (e.g., paralegal, legal assistant, or secretary) may not sign the name of a qualified practitioner or other authorized signatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'Just as signing the name of another person on paper does not serve as the signature of the person whose name is written, typing the electronic signature of another person is not a valid signature by that person.' TMEP § 611.01(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of improper signature on trademark filings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the signature on a trademark application or other submission fails to comply because it was entered by someone other than the named signatory or not signed by a proper person, then the submission is improperly executed, cannot be relied upon to support registration, and normally renders the application void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by rulemaking and precedent (e.g., In re Dermahose Inc., Ex parte Hipkins, In re Cowan). The integrity of the federal trademark registration process is adversely affected by impermissibly signed filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner certifications when presenting papers (37 C.F.R. § 11.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner, when presenting any paper to the USPTO, certifies that statements made on the practitioner's own knowledge are true and that statements based on information and belief are believed to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner also certifies that, after a reasonable inquiry, (i) the paper is not presented for an improper purpose; (ii) legal contentions are warranted by law or nonfrivolous argument; (iii) factual contentions have evidentiary support or are likely to after investigation; and (iv) denials of factual contentions are warranted or reasonably based on lack of information. See 37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(1)-(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable inquiry requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who presents any paper to the USPTO certifies that the practitioner has conducted an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances that supports the factual assertions set forth in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to perform a reasonable inquiry (e.g., not verifying use-in-commerce or authenticity of specimens) may constitute a rules violation and supports disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO.gov account sponsorship rules (Trademark Verified USPTO.gov Account Agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified attorneys are permitted to sponsor support staff who are directly employed by the attorney, the attorney's law firm, or the attorney's company, provided the support staff works under the attorney's supervision; sponsoring attorneys agree that they will not attempt to sponsor any foreign or domestic company, group, client, agent, attorney or other practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring prohibited persons (e.g., foreign firm employees not under direct supervision) violates the Verified Account Agreement and may lead to revocation of sponsorship privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision requirement for sponsored support staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsored support staff must be directly employed by and work under the supervision of the sponsoring attorney; persons not under the attorney's direct supervision or not employees of the firm may not be sponsored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring persons who are not supervised or not employees is a violation; the sponsor remains responsible for ensuring compliance with USPTO rules (e.g., signature rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: TEAS DIRECT signature contemporaneity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'DIRECT' signature option offered by TEAS requires the filer to enter the signature on the declaration contemporaneously with the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filings show they were filed from a different location (e.g., IP addresses from India) or signatures were entered by others, that indicates noncompliance with the contemporaneous signature requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall provide competent representation, which includes adequately reviewing trademark applications for which the practitioner serves as attorney of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence includes identifying issues such as specimens that appear inauthentic or do not demonstrate use in commerce, duplicate or redundant applications, and misstatements or clerical errors. Failing to identify such issues supports a finding of incompetence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence in representing clients (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must act with reasonable diligence in representing a client, including adequate review of filings and implementing procedures to ensure compliance with USPTO signature requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of failing diligence: inadequate review of applications, failing to ensure sponsored staff complied with signature rules, and sponsoring prohibited persons for USPTO.gov accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm supervisory obligations for non-practitioner assistants (37 C.F.R. § 11.503(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must make reasonable efforts to ensure the firm has measures giving reasonable assurance that the conduct of non-practitioner assistants is compatible with the professional obligations of the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes establishing procedures to verify authenticity of specimens, signatures, and that persons preparing/filing applications are authorized and properly supervised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assisting unauthorized practice of law (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not assist non-licensed persons in practicing before the USPTO; allowing unauthorized persons to prepare and file trademark applications under the attorney's credentials violates this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting a foreign firm without U.S.-licensed attorneys to prepare and file applications using the practitioner's name is an example of assisting unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to respond fully to OED Requests for Information (37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must respond fully to a Request for Information and Evidence (RFI) issued by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline; knowingly failing to respond fully is a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withholding requested documents (e.g., emails) deprives OED of important evidence and can be charged as misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct involving dishonesty or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty or misrepresentation, such as allowing filings to bear the practitioner's credentials to create the appearance of adequate review when none occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include allowing another to sign applicant declarations or to file applications that falsely appear to have been personally verified by the attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to USPTO integrity (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice or the integrity of the USPTO trademark examination and registration processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing or facilitating filings that undermine the authenticity of the register (e.g., impermissibly signed applications, inauthentic specimens) falls within this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney suspended may be granted limited recognition for a defined short period (here, thirty (30) days) to conclude work on behalf of clients on matters pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such work cannot be concluded within the limited-recognition period, the attorney must advise clients so they may make other arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on USPTO.gov account access during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: During suspension and until reinstated, the respondent shall not apply for, obtain, use, have name added to, verify, or sponsor any USPTO.gov or USPTO electronic system accounts used to prepare or file documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to the respondent; the respondent is prohibited from accessing or assisting others to use such accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation monitoring requirements (searches and reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: While on probation, respondent must (i) conduct at least monthly searches of TESS (or replacement) for applications identifying him as attorney of record and promptly inform the USPTO Office of Trademark Examination Policy of each filing identifying him that was made without his knowledge or consent; and (ii) submit at least quarterly written reports to the OED Director stating completion of monthly searches and reporting results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must state either that no unauthorized filings were found or provide copies of correspondence sent to OTEP regarding unauthorized filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to identify and declare filings not personally signed
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must, within twenty-one (21) days of the Final Order, send a letter listing all applications and other trademark documents on which he is the named signatory but where he did not sign the application or document, accompanied by a declaration/affidavit per 28 U.S.C. § 1746 stating that he did not sign the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list should include document type, filing date, and application serial number or registration number, and is to include the 174 applications in question and any others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with USPTO inquiries into improper filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall cooperate fully with the USPTO in any present or future inquiry made into improper filings by the foreign firm or any persons/entities with whom respondent worked in connection with trademark documents submitted to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation includes producing correspondence, records, and facilitating investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for reinstatement — CLE and TMEP review
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of being reinstated, respondent must provide a declaration/affidavit that he has successfully completed 3 hours of continuing legal education credit on trademark practice before the USPTO and that he has reviewed thoroughly all provisions of the TMEP, including USPTO signature requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations must comply with 28 U.S.C. § 1746 and be submitted to the OED Director as part of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order publicly (including the OED FOIA Reading Room) and shall publish a notice materially consistent with the Final Order in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice will summarize the misconduct, the suspension and probation, and specify the rules violated to inform practitioners and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of USPTO allowable costs (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of probation, respondent shall pay in full the USPTO's allowable costs described in 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 incurred in connection with the institution, prosecution, and dismissal of the formal disciplinary proceeding within sixty (60) days of being informed in writing of such costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay costs as required may affect reinstatement and compliance with the Final Order.
